title: duplicate-ingest-signals-causing-billing-overcount-and-throttle-misfires
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers reported unexpected spikes in invoiceable usage and intermittent 429s on low-traffic routes. Investigation shows duplicated usage events entering the billing pipeline and double-counts applied to per-key/per-org/per-route windows, which in turn caused the policy engine to prematurely throttle healthy clients.

Symptoms observed: duplicate usage rows in post-aggregation table, spiky meter cardinality for route-level buckets, and correlation between time-of-replay and increased 429 rate for routes that were previously under threshold. Affected window granularity: 1m and 1h quota windows; duplicates often arrived within the same minute window and were not collapsed.

Root cause hypothesis (current): The ingest path from API proxy -> ingestion-aggregator -> billing-collector relied on an idempotency key that was inconsistently populated by older SDKs and some internal proxies. Combined with Kafka at-least-once delivery and a recent change to the protobuf schema (serializer v2) that altered how request_id was encoded, certain events lost a stable dedupe key. Additionally the collector used a short-lived in-memory LRU deduper with a TTL of 30s, which is insufficient when consumer restarts or partition rebalances cause replay within the same billing window. The rate policy engine increments counters using the raw event stream without a second-stage dedupe, so duplicates immediately affect enforcement.

Immediate mitigations (implemented):
- Turned on shadow dedupe in billing-collector to reject obvious duplicates (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/482) — applied to staging.
- Rolled back the serializer change to preserve request_id encoding on the ingestion side (ops rollback commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/commit/6f4e9b2).
- Temporarily extended LRU dedupe TTL from 30s to 5m to cover rebalances (config change deployed to collector-asg).

Longer-term plan:
1) Server-side canonical event_id: compute event_uuid = sha256(org_id + route_id + canonical_payload_hash + client_timestamp) at the API proxy before emission. Store this stable id with every usage event. (owner: Marco, estimate 3).
2) Strong dedupe at billing-collector using persistent Redis-based dedupe index with TTL aligned to longest billing window; ensure dedupe idempotency survives consumer restarts (owner: billing team, estimate 5).
3) SDK upgrade: require request_id header and add deterministic generation helper; add migration plan for older SDK versions (owner: SDK team, cross-team effort).
4) Rate policy engine change: make enforcement decisions on deduped aggregates only; introduce a shadow-pass that verifies enforcement would be correct before applying in production (owner: policy-engine, estimate 3).
5) Add end-to-end tests that simulate Kafka replay and partition rebalances to assert dedupe correctness and throttle stability (owner: qa, estimate 2).

Telemetry & validation: dashboards/queries created:
- Billing duplicates view: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage/dup-detection?org=all
- Example SQL to enumerate suspect duplicates: https://docs.redwood.ai/queries/dup-detection.sql
- Customer impact report spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/billing-dup-2026-03.xlsx

Communication: Drafted customer-facing notes for impacted customers with credits to be issued for overcharges. Legal and finance looped in.

Open questions/risks:
- Potential edge cases in event_uuid generation for extremely high-cardinality payloads (payload hashing cost).
- Risk of false dedupe when client_timestamp precision is coarse; mitigations include payload hash plus sequence if present.
- Need coordination with Dedicated/Private deployments for schema changes.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Initial report from SOC: multiple billing anomalies for 3 enterprise tenants. Assigned to Marco.
2026-03-02 - Reproduced duplicate rows in staging ingestion with a synthetic Kafka replay test (see runbook gist: https://gist.github.com/mliu/dup-replay).
2026-03-03 - PR opened for shadow dedupe in billing-collector: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/482. Running in staging for 24h with no false positives so far.
2026-03-05 - Discovered serializer v2 commit that changed request_id encoding; initiated rollback (proxy commit 6f4e9b2).
2026-03-07 - Ops: extended in-memory dedupe TTL to 5m as stopgap. Monitoring 429s and invoice deltas closely.
2026-03-09 - Finance: preparing credits.csv for impacted customers; initial estimate of overbilled amount ~ $12.3k across 4 customers.
2026-03-10 - Design review for long-term dedupe approach scheduled; infra implications for Redis keyspace discussed.
review_feedback: PM (Lina Gomez): prioritize customer credits and communicate timeline; minimize rollout blast radius for dedupe index.
Security (Omar Khan): ensure event_uuid does not contain PII; prefer SHA256 over raw concatenation. Confirm KMS/HSM usage if needed.
Data Eng (Priya Raman): persistent dedupe will increase Redis ops; we should benchmark before enabling for all orgs.
next_steps: Merge and promote billing/pull/482 to prod behind feature flag (Marco) - target 2026-03-12.
Implement event_uuid generation in proxy and add to schema (owner: proxy team) - dep: SDK coordination.
Create Redis dedupe prototype and run load test for peak throughput (owner: infra) - target 2026-03-18.
Prepare customer communications and finalize credits for impacted accounts (owner: finance/customer-success) - target 2026-03-15.
